techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Lightweight woven cotton, satin, linen, or upcycled fabric

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Lightweight woven cotton, satin, linen, or upcycled fabric
One fabric strip measuring 27.5" x 6"
Elastic band
Thread

steps.title: Step 1: Cut - Prepare
steps.content:
You will need a long strip of fabric and a piece of elastic and scissors.
You’ll also need pins or clips, a bodkin, a fabric marker, a ruler.
The fabric is 5 × 20 inches (about 12 × 50 cm). The elastic is about 7 inches (18 cm) long.
Fold the fabric in half, right sides together.
Mark a 1 cm seam allowance along the edge.

tip.text: Use a rotary cutter and ruler to keep the strip edges straight and ensure the finished scrunchie has an even shape.

steps.title: Step 2: Sew the Short Edge
steps.content:
Align the two short edges with right side
Sew 2–3 stitches, then backstitch to secure.
Continue sewing forward and remember backstitch at the end to secure
Open the seam and press it flat.

tip.text: Make sure the fabric is not twisted before sewing the ends together, or the finished scrunchie will have an uneven shape.

steps.title: Step 3: Sew the Long Edge
steps.content:
Roll the top layer of fabric as shown.
Wrap the two edges of the bottom layer around the rolled fabric.
Align the long edges and secure with pins.
Sew along the long edge using a straight stitch.
Sew 2–3 stitches, then backstitch to secure.
Continue sewing forward as usual.and remove the pins as you sew.
Be careful not to sew into the rolled fabric inside.
Gently pull the rolled fabric inside as you sew.
Leave an opening of about 5 cm (2 in).
Backstitch at the end to secure.

tip.text: Be careful not to accidentally catch the inner fabric layers in the seam, as this will prevent the tube from turning correctly.

steps.title: Step 4: Turn the Tube
steps.content:
Turn the fabric tube right side out through the opening.
Smooth the fabric edges and press them flat.

tip.text: Hold both elastic ends securely while threading to prevent one end from slipping back inside the fabric tube.

steps.title: Step 5: Insert the Elastic
steps.content:
Attach the elastic to a measuring tape.
Pull it through the fabric tube.
Tie both ends together tightly.
Gently pull to check the stretch and knot.
Trim the excess, leaving about 1 cm.

tip.text: Hold both elastic ends securely while threading to prevent one end from slipping back inside the fabric tube.

steps.title: Step 6: Close the opening
steps.content:
Tuck the raw edges inside and align them neatly.
Backstitch at the beginning and end to secure.
Topstitch close to the edge to close the opening.
Trim the excess thread.
Adjust the fabric so the gathers are evenly distributed.

tip.text: Hold both elastic ends securely while threading to prevent one end from slipping back inside the fabric tube.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Cotton, quilting cotton, linen, or upcycled fabric scraps

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Cotton, quilting cotton, linen, or upcycled fabric scraps
Polyester fiberfill or foam filling
Hand sewing needle
Thread

steps.title: Step 1: Cut - Prepare
steps.content:
You will need main fabric, stuffing and scissors.
You’ll also need pins or clips, a bodkin, a fabric marker, a ruler.
Cut 2 main fabric pieces, each measuring 17 × 17 cm. The finished size will be 15 × 15 cm.
You can adjust the size to fit your mug, but make sure your cutting size is about 2 cm larger in both length and width than the finished size.
On the wrong side of the fabric, mark a 1 cm seam allowance along all four edges.
On the right side, measure 5 cm (2 inches) inward from each edge and draw a smaller square in the center.
Leave two openings on the same side of the inner and outer squares, each about 4 cm long.

tip.text: Use a quilting ruler and fabric marker to keep all sides perfectly square for a more professional finished coaster.

steps.title: Step 2: Sew the main piece
steps.content:
Place the two main fabric pieces right sides together.
Secure all four fabric corners with pins.
Align the center of the presser foot with the stitching line.
Sew 2–3 stitches, then backstitch to secure.
Continue sewing along the marked line, remember backstitch at the end to secure the seam.
When you reach the corner, leave the needle down in the fabric. Then lift the presser foot, pivot the fabric, lower the presser foot, and continue sewing.
Trim the corners carefully without cutting into the stitches. This helps the corners lie flatter when turned right side out.
Turn the fabric right side out.
If the corners are difficult to turn, gently push them out with a chopstick or a blunt tool. Be careful not to push too hard or pierce the fabric.

tip.text: Beginners often forget to leave a turning gap or make it too small, making it difficult to turn the coaster right side out.

steps.title: Step 3: Sew the inner square
steps.content:
Topstitch along the inner square, starting with a backstitch to secure the stitches.
Sew the inner square in the same way as the outer square, leaving an opening.
Trim the excess thread.
Now, let's stuff the small square area in the center first. You don't need to add too much stuffing here.
Sew the opening of the inner square closed
Then, stuff the outer border through the outer opening,

tip.text: Do not pull the corners too aggressively, as this can stretch the opening or distort the shape of the coaster.

steps.title: Step 4: Close the opening
steps.content:
Use a hand sewing needle to close the opening along the outer edge, bringing the needle up from between the two layers of fabric.
On the edge of the top fabric, take a small stitch from right to left.
Take a corresponding stitch on the bottom fabric directly below.
Continue taking stitches, alternating top and bottom, until the opening is completely closed.
Pull the thread to bring the fabric edges together
Finally, tie off the thread with a knot, then bury the thread tail inside the fabric.
Give it a gentle press to remove any fabric maker and to help the overall shape look more even.

tip.text: Overstuffing is a common mistake and can cause the coaster to wobble instead of sitting flat on a table.

techPack.title: Main Fabric
techPack.description: Cotton, quilting cotton, canvas, linen, or upcycled fabric

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Cotton, quilting cotton, canvas, linen, or upcycled fabric
Two outer fabric pieces measuring 7.87 inches x 3.54 inches
Two lining fabric pieces measuring 7.87 inches x 3.54 inches
Zipper
Thread
Sewing clips or pins

steps.title: Step 1: Cut  - Prepare
steps.content:
You will need main fabric, fusible interfacing, a zipper and scissors.
Cut 2 main fabric pieces and 2 interfacing pieces, each measuring 10 × 8 inches (about 25 × 20 cm).
Fuse the interfacing to the wrong side of the main fabric pieces.
Trim off any excess interfacing around the edges.

tip.text: Stack the fabric layers and cut them together to ensure all pouch pieces are exactly the same size.

steps.title: Step 2: Sew the zipper
steps.content:
Fold the two fabric pieces in half and press to create a crease.
Sandwich the zipper between the fabric layers and pin along the zipper tape.
Sew 2–3 stitches forward, then backstitch to secure.
Continue sewing along the edges, removing the pins as you go.
Remember to backstitch at the end to secure.
Turn the fabrics open and topstitch along the zipper edge.
Repeat the same process for the other side of the zipper.

tip.text: Make sure both zipper sides are aligned evenly before stitching, otherwise the pouch may become twisted or uneven when finished.

steps.title: Step 3: Sew around the edges
steps.content:
Open the zipper halfway so you can turn the pouch right side out later.
Mark a 2–3 inch (5–7 cm) opening for turning.
Align the edges and pin around all four sides.
Align the center of the presser foot with the stitching line.
Sew 2–3 stitches, then backstitch to secure.
Continue sewing along the edge, remember backstitch at the end to secure the seam.
When you reach the corner, leave the needle down in the fabric. Then lift the presser foot, pivot the fabric, lower the presser foot and continue sewing.

tip.text: Press the fabric away from the zipper before topstitching for a cleaner and more professional finish.

steps.title: Step 4: Turn right side out
steps.content:
Trim the corners carefully without cutting into the stitches. This helps the corners lie flatter when turned right side out.
Turn the pouch right side out through the opening gap.
Topstitch close to the edge to close the opening.
And that’s it! Our zipper pouch is finished and ready to use!

tip.text: Always open the zipper before sewing the pouch closed, otherwise it may be impossible to turn the pouch right side out.

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Woven or upcycled fabric
Width 59": 0.75 yd
Width 45": 0.75 yd
Outer bag: 2 pieces (according to the template)
Lining: 2 pieces (according to the template)
Shoulder straps: 2 pieces (according to the template)
All pieces include a 0.4" seam allowance unless otherwise noted.
Matching sewing thread
Pins or sewing clips
Fabric marker or tailor's chalk
Measuring tape
Scissors or rotary cutter
Iron and ironing board

steps.title: Step 1: Cut  - Prepare
steps.content:
To make this bag, we will be using a few essential sewing techniques: The standard straight stitch, edgestitching and topstitching. Join the straps together using an edgestitch and a topstitch. Boxing the corners: Cut the corners and sew the edges together
First, prepare main & lining fabric, download and print our bag pattern
Then, mark and cut out a triangle at the bottom corners of the pattern
Use the bag pattern to cut 2 main pieces and 2 lining pieces
At each bottom corner, cut out a pointed triangle as shown
Place the two main (/lining) pieces with right sides together, and pin them along the outer edges

tip.text: Transfer all notch and alignment marks before cutting to make assembling the outer bag and lining easier.

steps.title: Step 2: Sew the bottom seams
steps.content:
Select the straight stitch setting. Set the stitch length dial to 2 for a balanced, medium-length stitch
Bring the edges of the bottom triangle together (right sides facing)
Align the edges evenly and sew a straight line across
Repeat this process for the three remaining bottom corners

tip.text: Make sure the right sides are facing each other before sewing, or the seams will be visible on the outside of the bag.

steps.title: Step 3: Sew the main bag
steps.content:
*Remember to backstitch at the beginning of every seam to secure your stitches
Sew all the way around the bag along the pinned line, removing the pins as you go
When sewing the curved bottom, leave the needle down in the fabric, lift the presser foot, pivot the fabric, and continue sewing
Backstitch at the end of the seam to secure your stitches too

tip.text: Backstitch at both ends of the turning opening to prevent the seam from opening further during turning.

steps.title: Step 4: Sew the lining
steps.content:
Sew the lining exactly like the main bag by sewing the bottom corners and all the way around
Sew all the way around the bag, leaving a 10cm (4") gap unsewn at the bottom

tip.text: Clip the curved seam allowances carefully without cutting into the stitching to help the top edge lie flat after turning.

steps.title: Step 5: Join the bag and lining
steps.content:
Here is the finished main bag
Here is the lining, with the gap left unsewn at the bottom
Turn the lining right side out
Insert the lining into the main bag, ensuring the corners are perfectly aligned
Pin all the way around the edges of the bag opening & straps to hold layers securely in place
Pin two layers together along the bag opening and straps on both front and back of the bag
Sew along these pinned lines
Sew all the way around the opening and straps, removing the pins as you go

tip.text: Press the top edge thoroughly before topstitching to achieve a clean, professional-looking finish.

steps.title: Step 6: Sew the bottom lining gap closed
steps.content: Fold the raw edges of the turning hole inward and edgestitch to close

tip.text: Keep both straps exactly the same length so the finished tote hangs evenly when carried.

steps.title: Step 7: Pressing
steps.content: Roll the opening and straps seams to the very edge, then press flat to set the shape

tip.text: Fold the seam allowance evenly before stitching so the closed opening blends neatly with the rest of the lining.

steps.title: Step 8: Sewing the Strap
steps.content:
Fold the raw edge of the strap inward 1cm and pin it in place
Slide the raw edge of the remaining strap inside the folded end you just made
Sew 2 parallel lines: Edgestitch 1mm from the edge & Topstitch 5mm from the edge
Remember to backstitch at the beginning and end of your seams
Trim the excess thread

tip.text: Fold the seam allowance evenly before stitching so the closed opening blends neatly with the rest of the lining.

steps.title: Step 9: Edge stitching
steps.content: Edgestitch 1mm from the edge around the bag opening and the straps

tip.text: Fold the seam allowance evenly before stitching so the closed opening blends neatly with the rest of the lining.

techPack.title: Materials Needed
techPack.description:
Woven or upcycled fabric
Width 59": 0.5 yd
Width 45": 0.5 yd
Neck pillow body: 2 pieces (according to the template)
All pieces include a 0.4" seam allowance.
Polyester fiberfill
Matching sewing thread
Pins or sewing clips
Fabric marker or tailor's chalk
Scissors or rotary cutter
Turning tool or chopstick
Hand-sewing needle
Iron and ironing board

steps.title: Step 1: Cut  - Prepare
steps.content:
Today, we’re going to sew a comfort neck pillow.
You will need main fabric, stuffing and scissors.
You’ll also need pins or clips, a bodkin, a fabric marker, a ruler.
Prepare the neck pillow pattern in the dimensions shown.
Place the pattern on the fabric and trace around the outline.
Cut out the two pillow pieces along the marked line.

tip.text: Transfer any center or alignment marks from the pattern before cutting to make matching the curved edges easier during sewing.

steps.title: Step 2: Sew along the edges
steps.content:
Place the two main fabric pieces right sides together and pin around the edges.
Mark a 6–8 cm opening along the outer curve for turning and stuffing.
Start sewing from one end of the opening.
Sew 2–3 stitches forward, then backstitch to secure.
Continue sewing along the edges, removing the pins as you go.
Remember to backstitch at the end to secure.

tip.text: Remember to leave the turning opening unsewn and backstitch at both ends so the seam stays secure during turning.

steps.title: Step 3: Turn right side out
steps.content:
Turn the pillow right side out through the opening.
Stuff the pillow evenly with fiberfill until it reaches your desired firmness.

tip.text: Clip close to the curved seams without cutting through the stitching, or the seam may split when the pillow is turned.

steps.title: Step 4: Close the opening
steps.content:
Fold the raw edges inward and align them neatly.
Use a ladder stitch to close the opening.
Pull the thread tight, tie a knot and hide the thread tail.
And that’s it! Our comfort neck pillow is finished and ready to use!

tip.text: Use a blunt turning tool to gently push out the curved sections without damaging the fabric.
